projects.title: Robin
projects.subtitle: A gesture-based instrument for live performance

hero.image_alt: Robin custom physical instrument with copper touch pads and ESP32 microcontroller
hero.caption: Robin, a custom instrument for a live dialogue between performer and system.

projects.summary: Robin is a custom percussion instrument that turns touch and movement into a shared musical process between performer and system.
projects.project_thesis: The project asks how much of a musical performance can be controlled—and what new possibilities appear when the instrument makes choices of its own.
projects.visitor_experience: Touch sets rhythms in motion, while the performer's movement changes their pace and texture. The instrument introduces variation; the performer listens, responds, and shapes what happens next.

projects.title: A Machine for Misunderstanding
projects.subtitle: A text-to-sound experiment on communication and interpretation

hero.image_alt: A Machine for Misunderstanding modular synthesizer interface and 3D VAD vector visualization
hero.caption: A system that translates written language into modular sound.

projects.summary: A text-to-sound system and listening study exploring what changes when emotional language passes through a machine.
projects.project_thesis: When words are translated into sound, what carries through—and what is changed or misunderstood? The project explores this question through a machine-mediated exchange and a listening study.
projects.visitor_experience: Participants exchange short texts through a system that turns language into modular sound. One person sends a message; another listens to its sonic translation and describes what they hear. Comparing intention with perception makes each step of the exchange part of the work.

projects.title: Listener
projects.subtitle: An acoustic feedback system that listens to its environment

hero.image_alt: Listener modular patch signal flow diagram with 119 active modules in VCV Rack
hero.caption: The current VCV Rack patch for capturing, transforming, and returning room sound.

projects.summary: Listener records sounds from a room, transforms them, and plays them back into the same space—so each response becomes part of what the system hears next.
projects.project_thesis: What does it mean for a system to listen when the sounds it has already heard shape what it notices next? Listener explores this question through an evolving acoustic feedback loop.
projects.visitor_experience: A microphone picks up sounds already present in the space. Listener captures a brief fragment, reshapes it, and plays it back into the room. That response becomes part of the next listening moment, allowing the sound environment to change over time. Field recordings are still in progress.
